title: Rack fifteen pool balls tight on the foot spot, then lift the triangle off without disturbing them
instruction: Rack the balls tight on the foot spot and take the rack away.
context: Racking is how every game of 8-ball starts. Anyone who has played pool at a bar, at home or in a rec room has racked the balls themselves, and a loose rack (gaps between balls) spoils the break. A wooden triangle is roomier than the pack: about 270 mm inside from the head ball to the rear, against 255 mm for fifteen touching 2 1/4 in balls. Balls dropped in stand apart, so the racker presses the pack into the triangle's apex while setting the head ball on the foot spot, then lifts the triangle off without moving any ball: a few mm of sideways motion while the bars still touch the balls rolls them apart.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the table. A 56 x 62 cm patch of green worsted pool cloth (3 mm) lies on the table, centred at x 43, y 0, standing for the foot end of a pool table's bed; the foot spot, a 2.5 cm white paper disc, is at x 46, y 0. On the cloth: a wooden 8-ball triangle rack for 2 1/4 in balls (three bars 15 mm thick and 3.2 cm tall, 227 g; inside 10 5/8 in (27.0 cm) from the head ball's corner to the middle of the rear bar), apex pointing away from the robot (+x), rear bar toward it with its centre at x 22.6. In it, fifteen 57.15 mm phenolic pool balls (165 g) in legal 8-ball order by rows from the apex: 1; 9, 2; 10, 8, 3; 11, 7, 14, 4; 5, 13, 15, 6, 12 (stripes shown as lighter solids). They are loose: every touching pair stands 2 mm apart; the 1-ball touches both side bars at the apex, its centre 1.5 cm past the spot (x 47.5); the rear row is 7.8 mm off the rear bar. Arms start in the ready pose.
scoring: The table's long axis runs along x; the head of the table and its head string are at +x (away from the robot). Latched 0 for the trial: once the rack's lowest point is 2 mm above the cloth, any ball's centre moves more than 3 mm sideways (horizontally) before the rack is set down away from the pack; if the rack comes back down flat on the cloth first, the reference is taken again at its next rise. Otherwise, at the end: 0 the head (1) ball's centre more than 10 mm from the spot's centre; 0.25 within 10 mm; 0.5 that and the rack taken away: set down on the table, still, with every part at least 50 mm horizontally (seen from above) from every ball; 0.75 that, at least 24 of the 30 touching pairs within 0.5 mm (feeler gauge; sim: centre distance minus 57.15 mm), and the pack facing the head of the table: the line from the 15 ball centres' centroid to the head ball within 5 degrees of the long axis, pointing toward +x, and the line fitted through the 5 rear-row centres within 3 degrees of square to that axis; 1.0 that, all 30 pairs within 0.5 mm, the head ball within 5 mm of the spot, all balls still, and no gripper point within 30 mm of any ball. Real rig: two overhead photos against a grid on the cloth, one just before the rack starts to rise and one after it is set down (0 if any ball centre moved more than 3 mm between them); the second photo also gives the head ball's distance from the spot, the rack's horizontal clearance and both orientation angles; only after both photos, a 0.5 mm feeler gauge for each of the 30 touching pairs: a leaf held vertical, square to the line between the two centres, is lowered into the gap midway between them; two spheres are closest at their equators on that line, so the pair is within 0.5 mm unless the leaf passes the equators and reaches the cloth (the leaf must not push either ball). Success when 1.0 holds for 1 s; otherwise scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Put the rack back with its rear bar centre at x 22.6 and the balls in the order above, loose: each pair 2 mm apart (a 2 mm shim card between neighbours, then removed), the 1-ball against both side bars, its centre 15 mm past the spot. Check that no ball is touching the rear bar.
fidelity: Full-size balls (57.15 mm, 165 g) and rack. Rigid spheres; angular damping (10/s) stands in for the cloth's rolling resistance, which PhysX lacks. Friction ball-ball 0.06, ball-cloth 0.20, ball-wood 0.30 (estimates); contact offset 0.1 mm. demo() as shipped: 5/5 at 1.0 on one host (widest gap 0.25 mm, head ball 4.0 mm). Tightening is the real difficulty: 6 trials of demo variants left widest gaps of 0.25-0.80 mm (3 under 0.5 mm). The cloth is a patch, not a full table.
